docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
pydantic-schemaforms turns a Pydantic model into a server-rendered HTML form, and validates what comes back with the same model.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, html, render_form_html_async


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    name: str = Field(title='Full name', min_length=2)
    email: str = Field(title='Email', ui_element='email')


app = FastAPI()
RENDER_OPTIONS = {'include_framework_assets': True, 'asset_mode': 'cdn'}


@app.get('/signup', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def show_signup():
    return await render_form_html_async(SignupForm, submit_url='/signup', **RENDER_OPTIONS)


@app.post('/signup', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def submit_signup(request: Request):
    result = SignupForm.validate(await request.form(), submit_url='/signup', **RENDER_OPTIONS)
    if not result.is_valid:
        return await result.render_with_errors_async()

    name = result.data['name']
    return html(t'<p>Thanks for signing up, {name}!</p>')

That's a complete FastAPI app: a styled signup form, browser and server validation, errors shown next to each field with the user's input kept, and the validated data as a plain dictionary. A Flask version is the same model with render_form_html() and request.form.

Features

  • One model for everything. The form, its validation, the validated data and, with as_api_model(), a typed JSON API all come from one Pydantic class.
  • Inputs from types. str, int, date, bool, Enum, Literal, EmailStr and more pick their input; Field(ui_element=...) chooses any of 40+ others (currency, tags, rating, code editor, file upload, ...).
  • Complex forms by nesting. Sub-forms, optional sub-forms and repeating lists, shown as sections, tabs, columns, an accordion or a step wizard with one layout= argument. Data and errors come back nested like the model.
  • Bootstrap, Material or plain HTML, with assets inlined, linked from a CDN or left to your page.
  • Escaped by construction. All HTML is built with Python 3.14 t-strings and an escaping processor.
  • Accessibility-tested. Every input, layout and error state is checked with axe-core against WCAG 2.0–2.2 A and AA rules on every pull request.
  • More when you need it: live validation over HTMX, CSV import into an editable table, CSRF protection, rule-based validators and plugin hooks for your own inputs.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add "pydantic-schemaforms[fastapi]"     # or [flask]
pip install "pydantic-schemaforms[fastapi]"

Requires Python 3.14+ (the library uses t-strings) and Pydantic 2.13+; tested on 3.14 and 3.15. Add the email extra if your forms use EmailStr.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
pydantic-schemaforms is a Python library for generating server-rendered HTML forms from Pydantic models.

It focuses on:

  • One Pydantic model for the form, its validation and its data
  • HTML that is escaped by construction, built with Python 3.14 t-strings
  • Sync (WSGI) and async (ASGI) rendering, tested with FastAPI and Flask
  • Offline-by-default asset delivery (vendored/inlined assets), with explicit opt-in for CDNs

If you're new, start with the Tutorial. The Reference lists every input, layout and option.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Other ways to build forms in Python web apps, and how pydantic-schemaforms differs. Pick the one that fits your stack.

docs.title: What this library is for
docs.text:
pydantic-schemaforms suits apps that render HTML on the server and already use, or want to use, Pydantic models:

  • One model for everything. The form, its validation, the validated data and, with as_api_model(), a JSON API share one Pydantic class.
  • Server-rendered. You get an HTML string. There is no JavaScript framework, no build step and no client-side state; the small scripts it adds (live formatting, the wizard, Add and Remove buttons) are optional enhancements.
  • Framework-agnostic. It works with any Python web framework that can return a string; the docs show FastAPI and Flask.
  • Escaped by construction. All HTML is built with t-strings and an escaping processor, so values are escaped structurally, not by remembering to.

It is not a good fit when your frontend is a single-page app that renders its own forms, or when you need a visual form designer.

docs.title: WTForms
docs.text:
WTForms is the long-standing framework-agnostic form library, used by Flask-WTF and Starlette-WTF. Forms are declared with WTForms' own field classes and validators, and you lay out the fields yourself in templates.

Choose WTForms when your app doesn't use Pydantic or you want full control of each field's markup in templates. Choose pydantic-schemaforms when you'd rather declare the form once as a Pydantic model and get the whole form, including nested sub-forms, lists and layouts, rendered for you.

docs.title: Django forms
docs.text: Django's forms, with ModelForm, are the natural choice inside Django, where they tie into the ORM, the admin and the template system. pydantic-schemaforms doesn't integrate with Django's ORM or admin; a Django adapter is on the Roadmap.

docs.title: JSON Schema form renderers in the browser
docs.text:
Libraries such as react-jsonschema-form render a form in the browser from a JSON Schema, which a Pydantic model can produce. They suit apps that already have a React frontend. The form is built by JavaScript on the client, and the server validates the posted JSON separately.

pydantic-schemaforms renders on the server, so the form arrives as HTML, works with plain form posts, and the same model validates the submission. Its get_pydantic_json_schema() output can still feed such a renderer if you need both.

docs.title: Writing the HTML by hand
docs.text: For one small form, a hand-written <form> and a Pydantic model to validate it is often enough. The work grows with each form: showing errors next to the right inputs, keeping submitted values, escaping them, labels and accessibility, nested data, repeating items and layouts. That is what this library does for you.

docs.title: [26.4.3] — 2026-10-29
docs.text: FormModel is now the only way to build a form: the builder API, the prebuilt forms, @form_validator and the React/Vue adapters are removed. Five Agent Skills ship inside the package, and a long list of form bugs is fixed. This is a breaking release; see docs/upgrading.md.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• React and Vue adapters removed. ReactJSONSchemaFormAdapter, VueFormulateAdapter, and their modules (integration.json_schema_form_adapter, integration.vue_formulate_adapter, and the integration.react/integration.vue shims) are deleted, along with the React/Vue-only helpers map_ui_element_to_framework and convert_validation_rules. They produced config blobs for client-side form libraries, outside this library's server-rendered scope, and had no examples or docs. For a JSON Schema of a form, use FormModel.get_json_schema(); for a plain Pydantic model, use FormModel.as_api_model(). (#248)
  • The builder API is removed; FormModel is the only way to build a form. FormBuilder, AutoFormBuilder, create_form_from_model, create_login_form, create_registration_form, create_contact_form, render_form_page, FormIntegration, handle_form and handle_form_async are deleted, along with ModernFormRenderer, FormDefinition and FormSection (which only existed to render builder forms) and the integration.builder/adapters/sync/async_support modules. The builder rendered through its own path, so it never got layout=, the wizard, nested sub-forms, model_list or DataTableLayout. To upgrade: declare a FormModel (or build one at runtime with Pydantic's create_model(..., __base__=FormModel)), render it with render_form_html() and handle submissions with FormModel.validate() and result.render_with_errors(). See docs/upgrading.md. Importing any removed name raises an ImportError that names its replacement. (#255)
  • @form_validator is removed. It never ran: nothing called the methods it decorated, so cross-field checks written with it were silently skipped. Use Pydantic's @model_validator(mode="after") (its message lands in the form-wide _errors) or FormValidator.add_cross_field_rule. (#254)
  • DataTableLayout input names are namespaced by the embedding field. Cells, the CSV file input and the Load/Submit buttons used to have fixed names (rows[i].col, csv_file, datatable_action), so two tables on one page overwrote each other. They are now named under the field the table is embedded in (an employees field submits employees.rows[i].col, employees.csv_file, employees.datatable_action), and the default table id comes from the field name instead of the row model's class name. handle_import_post() and parse_submitted_rows() find their table in the submission themselves, so app code using them doesn't change. Code that reads those form keys directly, or builds test submissions by hand, must use the new names. When two tables share a row model, pass the new field= argument to say which one to read. (#253)

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Agent Skills ship inside the package. uvx library-skills --claude installs five skills into an app project, linked to the installed version: pydantic-schemaforms (build and fix forms, with references for inputs, complex forms, validation, data tables, security, rendering and extending), schemaforms-create (a new form from a description such as "create a login form", commented like a tutorial), schemaforms-convert (from Pydantic, dataclasses, JSON Schema, WTForms or Django), schemaforms-upgrade (from removed APIs) and schemaforms-document (docstrings, help text and a Markdown page for an app's forms). The single-file instructions from get_app_instructions() and the CLI are now built from the same sources, and their examples come from tested files. (#264)
  • Accessibility gate. The Playwright suite runs axe-core 4.14 against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA rules plus axe best practices on every example page under Bootstrap and Material, plus the validation page's error state, and fails on any serious or critical violation. axe-core is vendored for tests only (tests/playwright/vendor/, pinned by version and SHA-256); it is not shipped in the package. What is tested, the baseline the inputs meet, and what automated testing does not cover are in the new docs/reference/accessibility.md page and the README. This is testing, not a claim of ADA, Section 508 or WCAG conformance. (#246)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Two tabbed or accordion forms on one page no longer collide. Tab and accordion ids were numbered from tab-0/accordion-0 in every form, so the second form's tabs and panels controlled the first form's. Each layout now gets its own id prefix, and tab and accordion scripts only act inside their own layout (which also stops an outer tab hiding a nested tabbed sub-form). (#252)
  • Accordion fixes: under Bootstrap the open section rendered closed, and under plain HTML and Material clicking a section header submitted the form. (#252)
  • Invalid fields are announced. After a failed submit, a field's control gets aria-invalid="true" and an aria-describedby pointing at its error message, and at its help text whenever it has one, under Bootstrap, Material and plain HTML. Help and error elements now carry matching <id>-help / <id>-error ids. (#246)
  • DataTableLayout cells have accessible names. Each editable cell gets an aria-label such as "Email, row 3", since its column header is not a <label>. (#246)
  • The tags input's label names its text box. The visible text box now takes the field's id, so <label for=...> points at it, and it receives the aria-* wiring above. (#246)
  • The code editor's highlight layer no longer takes keyboard focus. It is aria-hidden, but Prism made it tabbable. (#246)
  • Contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) for tag chips, the code editor's property/tag syntax color and the "Rendered in" timing line. (#246)
  • The date picker toggle is a 24×24 px target (WCAG 2.2 target size). (#246)
  • Inputs are inferred from more field types. Without a ui_element, date, datetime, time, EmailStr and AnyUrl fields render as date, datetime-local, time, email and URL inputs; Enum and Literal fields render as a select with their values; and a list of either renders as a multiselect. Optional fields keep their input type instead of falling back to a text box. Previously an Enum field rendered an empty section (or a select with no options), so its choices had to be built by hand. (#258)
  • A fresh form shows the model's defaults. When no form_data is passed, every field starts at its default (an int = 1 shows 1, an Enum or Literal default is selected, a bool = True checkbox is ticked, default_factory values included). Passed data, such as a submission being re-rendered or an edit form, is still used as is. Previously defaults were never rendered, so they had to be passed in form_data by hand. (#258)
  • Validator messages are shown as written. A ValueError raised in a @field_validator or @model_validator shows its own message, without Pydantic's "Value error, " prefix. (#258)
  • Optional selects can be left empty. An Optional select gets an empty first choice, and submitting it validates to None, including for str-based enums. (#258)
  • An Enum field keeps its title when it matches the Enum class's name (Field(title="Size") on a Size enum), including inside list items; it used to fall back to the field name. (#258)
  • Material renders datetime fields as datetime-local, not the invalid datetime input type. (#258)
  • Pre-filling an Enum field selects its option. form_data holding an Enum member, as a database row or model_dump() does, used to leave the select (or radio) with nothing chosen. (#258)
  • A checkbox that defaults to True can be unticked. An unticked checkbox sends nothing, so validate() used to fill in the default and return True. In a form submission, a missing checkbox that has a default is now False; one without a default is still required, and nested JSON that omits it still gets the default. (#258)
  • An optional sub-form (Address | None) can be left empty. Its inputs are no longer required, and when every one of them is blank or still at its default, validate() returns None for it instead of field errors. (#258)
  • A currency input works on a Decimal, float or int field. The input formats what is typed as $1,234.50, which used to fail validation as "Input should be a valid decimal". In a form submission the symbol and thousands separators are now stripped first. (#258)
  • A float field accepts decimals in the browser. Number inputs always had step="1", so the browser refused 39.50. A float field now gets step="any", and multiple_of sets the step. (#258)
  • Material inputs carry the field's constraints. min_length, max_length, ge, le and pattern now become minlength, maxlength, min, max and pattern attributes under Material too, as they already did under Bootstrap and plain HTML. (#258)
  • MinLengthRule skips an empty value, like every other rule except RequiredRule and like its own client-side check. It used to reject "", so an optional field with a minimum length couldn't be left blank. (#258)

docs.title: [26.4.1] — 2026-10-12
docs.text: Complex forms are now built one way: nest FormModels as fields of a parent FormModel and pick a layout=. Data in and out is nested JSON. This is a breaking release; see docs/upgrading.md.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• Form-orchestration classes removed. TabbedLayout, ListLayout, SectionDesign, FormDesign, FormLayoutBase, and the form_layouts VerticalLayout/HorizontalLayout wrappers now raise FormLayoutRemovedError (a TypeError) when subclassed or called. The message contains the upgrade steps and points to the new "Upgrading to nested forms" section of the AI instructions.
  • Top-level VerticalLayout/HorizontalLayout now name the flex layout primitives from rendering/layout_engine.py, which the removed wrappers used to shadow.
  • pydantic_schemaforms.layouts (the deprecated re-export shim) is deleted.
  • FormModel.validate(flatten=...) removed. result.data is always nested like the model. Passing flatten raises a TypeError explaining this.
  • ValidationResult.errors is a nested error tree shaped like the data (errors["pets"][1]["name"]) instead of string-path keys (errors["pets[1].name"]). Container and form-wide messages use the reserved "_errors" key instead of "general".
  • layout="tabbed"/"side-by-side" group sub-forms. The field-name keyword heuristic and the two-fields-per-row pairing are gone; on a form with no sub-form fields these layouts raise ValueError. Several input_type="layout" fields no longer auto-render as tabs; pass layout="tabbed".
  • Unknown layout= values raise ValueError instead of rendering vertically.
  • Non-validation exceptions propagate from validate() instead of being shown on the form as errors["general"].
  • Renderer internals: RenderContext.all_errors is replaced by child_errors (the field's own error sub-tree), and render_field() takes the field's error node as error with no all_errors argument. get_nested_form_data, EnhancedFormRenderer._humanize_error_field, and FieldRenderer.extract_nested_errors_for_field are removed.
  • handle_form/handle_form_async with a model return nested data and a nested error tree. FormValidator.validate_pydantic_model() (which kept only the first segment of each error path) is removed.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Sub-form fields. A field typed as another FormModel (or Optional of one) renders as a titled section with inputs named address.city, with no ui_element needed. ui_collapsible/ui_collapsed render it as a <details> section that opens when it holds an error.
  • Grouped layouts: layout="tabbed", "side-by-side", and the new "accordion" arrange the parent's plain fields plus one group per sub-form, in declaration order (ui_order overrides). Re-rendering after a failed submit opens the first group that contains an error.
  • Step wizard: layout="wizard" shows the same groups one step at a time with a progress header and Back/Next. All steps are in one <form>, so one POST submits everything. Next runs the browser's validation on the current step; a re-render opens the first step with an error and marks the others. Options: wizard_options={"linear", "show_progress", "back_label", "next_label"} and Field(ui_step_title=...). Without JavaScript all steps show stacked.
  • Examples cover every layout, input, and validation, enforced by tests/test_examples_coverage.py and a browser test that loads every example page: the widget gallery shows every input type and alias with each of its options plus field-level options (ui_disabled, ui_readonly, icon, ...); /validation shows every Pydantic constraint, validator, rule class, and a cross-field rule failing on one form; /layouts takes the wizard options as query parameters; /employees/directory shows the read-only DataTableLayout options.
  • validate() takes the raw request form (Starlette FormData, Werkzeug MultiDict, (name, value) pairs) as well as nested dicts, keeping repeated values as lists. render_form_html(form_data=...) accepts the same.
  • render_with_errors(errors=...) re-renders with a different error tree, e.g. the result's own errors merged with a rule-based FormValidator's.
  • AI instructions now list every ui_options key per widget with its default, every field-level option, the rule classes and cross-field rules, the FormModel/ValidationResult API, every render option, and the asset helpers.
  • ValidationResult.error_list() (flat [{"loc": [...], "msg": ...}]) and ValidationResult.instance (the validated model).
  • list[FormModel] fields render as repeating sub-forms without ui_element="model_list".
  • LiveValidator.register_model_validator() registers sub-form and list-item fields under their input names (address.city, pets[].name).
  • validate_form_data is exported from the top-level package, as the validation guide already documented.
  • docs/complex_forms.md, a guide to composing forms and upgrading.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Decoding a submission compacts list indices instead of padding gaps with None: pets[0] and pets[2] decode to a two-item list, so an item removed without re-indexing still validates, and one field named like pets[500000000].name no longer makes the server allocate a list that long.
  • validation_response_headers, wrap_with_schemaforms_markers, read_asset_text, bootstrap_icons_css_content and bootstrap_icons_css_tag are exported from the top-level package; the docs and examples imported them from internal modules.
  • Removing every item of a repeating sub-form now fails its min_length instead of passing as the field's default (form submissions only; nested JSON that omits the key still gets the default).
  • Under layout="tabbed"/"accordion"/"wizard", Material forms no longer let the browser block submission on a required input in a hidden group with no visible message; the server re-renders with that group open.
  • A layout field's default_factory that raises is no longer silently swallowed (the table rendered empty); the error propagates.
  • radio and checkbox_group never showed the current value: a re-rendered form lost the user's choices. A combobox lost its value the same way.
  • A field declared ui_element="hidden" rendered a visible label (only ui_hidden=True produced a bare hidden input).
  • Custom date_format/time_format/datetime_format were not applied to ISO string values (JSON data), which showed as 2024-06-15 instead of the format.
  • The file input's preview script failed to parse (a # comment in JavaScript), so no preview appeared; it now shows file names as text, never as markup.
  • Material: the colour picker's hex readout (show_value) was missing, and a select with a placeholder had its label overlapping the placeholder text.
  • Switching tabs left the active class on the first panel.
  • Field(icon=...), like other non-Pydantic keywords, was silently dropped when any ui_* option was also passed.
  • Material forms' inline script failed to parse (a # comment in JavaScript), so its floating-label and field enhancements never ran.
  • Field() silently dropped any ui_* option it doesn't name as a parameter (such as ui_collapsible) when another ui_* option like ui_help_text was also passed. All ui_* options are now kept.
  • Validation errors now reach fields inside sub-forms and are namespaced per sub-form, so two sub-forms with the same field name no longer collide.
  • Library code no longer imports from the examples/ package or hard-codes the demo app's field names.
  • DataTableLayout.parse_submitted_rows() no longer turns cell values like "1" or "yes" into booleans before validation.
  • The documented FormConfig/TabbedLayout((...)) and HorizontalLayout(label_cols=...) recipes, which never worked, are replaced.
  • Several documentation examples that interpolated submitted values into HTML with f-strings now use html(t"...").

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• LiveValidator.register_model_validator partial-validation bug — previously called model_class.model_validate({field: value}) with only one field's data; if the model had other required fields, Pydantic raised ValidationError for them, causing all unrelated fields to produce is_valid=False with no errors even when the value was valid. Now uses __pydantic_validator__.validate_assignment(model_construct(), field_name, value) to validate each field in isolation, independent of sibling required fields.

  • LiveValidator.render_field_with_live_validation single-trigger limitation — the if/elif/elif chain for validate_on_blur / validate_on_input / validate_on_change silently dropped every trigger after the first truthy one. Changed to independent if checks so all enabled triggers combine into a single hx-trigger attribute (e.g. hx-trigger="blur, change" when both are True).

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Live-validation example — GET /live-validation demo route in the FastAPI example app shows a contact form with per-field HTMX validation on blur. Includes POST /validate/{field_name} HTMX endpoint using validation_response_headers() and GET /vendor/htmx.min.js to serve the vendored HTMX asset.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • FormModel.as_api_model() — new class method that returns a pure Pydantic BaseModel with ui_* rendering metadata stripped from json_schema_extra. Allows the same model class to serve both as an HTML form and as a typed FastAPI body / response_model without ui_element, ui_placeholder, etc. appearing in the OpenAPI/Swagger docs. Field(title=...), Field(examples=[...]), descriptions, and all validation constraints (min_length, ge, pattern, …) are fully preserved. Result is cached per subclass and safe to assign at module level (ContactSchema = ContactForm.as_api_model()).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Reduced SonarCloud code smells: extracted duplicate magic strings to named constants, prefixed unused parameters with _, renamed methods that shadowed class attributes, and merged nested if statements into compound conditions across multiple modules.

docs.title: [26.2.1] — 2026-05-17
docs.text: First production release. All public Quick Start code paths verified working end-to-end.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: • submit_url is now explicit across public form render APIs and no longer defaults silently. Calls that omit submit_url raise a clear ValueError, enforcing app-owned routing boundaries.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• HTMX live validation — LiveValidator, HTMXValidationConfig, and validation_response_headers() provide server-side field validation triggered by blur/input events via HTMX without page reloads.
  • Branch coverage — branch = true added to coverage configuration for deeper test quality.
  • HTML structural validation — tests/test_html_structural.py validates tag balance across all frameworks and field types.
  • HTTP integration tests — FastAPI TestClient and Flask test_client round-trip tests.
  • Property-based tests — Hypothesis suite covering arbitrary field names, labels, and frameworks.
  • Performance benchmarks — pytest-benchmark suite for small, medium, and large form rendering.
  • Playwright browser tests — End-to-end HTMX validation tests against a live FastAPI server (tests/playwright/), running in CI on Chromium.
  • macOS in CI matrix — Tests now run on ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, and macos-latest.
  • py.typed marker for PEP 561 compatibility.
  • Vendored assets (htmx, Bootstrap, Materialize, iMask) with sha256 manifest verification.
  • .gitattributes forcing LF line endings on vendored assets for cross-platform checksum stability.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• create_form_from_model crashed with any Pydantic model — AutoFormBuilder._build_from_model used the wrong parameter name (default_value instead of value) and compared against ... instead of PydanticUndefined; the sentinel leaked into json_schema_extra, causing PydanticSerializationError on every render call.
  • Windows path separator in test assertion caused CI failure on win32.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
The order to work through open enhancements and known bugs. Work top to bottom: each phase sets up the ones after it. GitHub issues hold the design detail for each item. This file only sets the order and says why.

Every item follows the "Examples must cover every layout, input, and validation" rule in CLAUDE.md: a feature isn't done until it's demonstrated on an example page under both Bootstrap and Material.

Last updated: 2026-10-29.

docs.title: Phase 1: Clear the ground
docs.text:
Small fixes and decisions that the later phases build on. Do these first so new features aren't layered on known bugs. Phase 1 ships as its own release.

All phase 1 items are done; they ship as release 26.4.3.

# Item Status Why now 1 #252 Fix fixed element IDs in tabbed and accordion layouts Done (#257) Two grouped forms on one page collide. Conditional fields (#237) and field groups (#241) both change the layout engine, so fix this before they land. Copy the wizard's ID-free, data-attribute approach. 2 #253 Fix two DataTables on one page colliding Done (#260) Cell and control names are fixed (rows[i].col, csv_file). Derive them from the embedding field's name. Small and self-contained. 3 #254 Remove or wire up @form_validator Done (#261) It's a top-level export that does nothing, so decorated checks never run. Removing it is breaking, so batch it with item 4 (#255) into one breaking release. 4 #255 Decide on FormBuilder and the prebuilt login, registration and contact forms (left open from #248) Done (#261) #248 closed when the React/Vue removal merged, but this half was never decided. The answer shapes #235 and #190: keep and document them as the "form without a model" path, or remove them and let JSON Schema import fill that role. 5 #246 Accessibility gate with axe-core Done (#262) Low effort. Landing it before the new widgets in phases 2 and 3 means each one is checked as it's built instead of fixed later. 6 #264 Ship library skills (library-skills.io) inside the package Done (#269) Lets uvx library-skills install version-matched agent guidance from the installed package, so AI agents stop suggesting removed APIs. Five skills: build and fix forms, create, convert, upgrade and document. Ships with the phase 1 release, right after the breaking removals in #254 and #255. 7 #258 Reorganize the documentation Done (#267) Do it with #147 or straight after it, so the new navigation is built once in the new tool. Content work (merging duplicate pages, shortening the README) can start before the tool is chosen. Docs aren't part of the package, so this doesn't hold up the phase 1 library release.

docs.title: Phase 2: Core form features
docs.text:
How phase 2 and later phases are grouped into releases is not decided yet.

The features people ask for most. Each one builds on the layout engine and the wizard that shipped in 26.4.1.

# Item Status Why in this order 8 #265 Rebuild the Material style on the shared rendering path Not started Material renders through its own parallel code path, so every widget and fix is done twice and Material keeps lagging (the Enum, constraint and step bugs fixed for #258 were all Material-only or Material-too). Do it before the phase 2 features so conditional fields, groups and display mode are built once. Also removes the vendored Materialize files it no longer uses. 9 #237 Conditional show/hide rules Not started The most common missing form feature. Needs the ID fix from phase 1. 10 #241 Field groups and grid widths in one model Not started Next layout change after #237, so show/hide rules can target a whole group. 11 #238 Read-only display mode Not started Supplies the display templates the wizard review step (#250) needs, and replaces the f-string confirmation pages users write today, which is an XSS risk. Must handle groups from #241. 12 #250 Wizard review step Not started Adds an opt-in final wizard step that shows everything entered before Submit, for example a job application. Builds on #238: reuse its per-input display formatting and escaping rather than writing a second set. Ships with a job-application wizard example. 13 #243 Draft autosave and unsaved-changes warning Not started Small vanilla-JS feature. Most useful once long forms and the wizard have conditional fields and groups. 14 #245 Testing helpers for app authors Not started Comes after the phase 2 features so the submission builders handle conditional fields, groups and display mode from the start.

docs.title: Phase 3: Inputs and data
docs.text:
New widgets and the server work behind them. All of them get checked by the accessibility gate from phase 1.

# Item Status Why in this order 15 #178 Mobile-friendly inputs Not started Start by re-auditing the issue: some Tier 2 items have shipped since July. Then do the remaining Tier 2 and Tier 3 items that fit the vanilla-JS pattern: OTP code, segmented control, stepper buttons, password strength meter, year picker. Skip Tier 5. 16 #242 Server-side upload validation and drag-and-drop Not started Covers the file drag-and-drop item from #178. The server half is bigger than the widget. 17 #239 Remote options for select and combobox Not started Reuses the HTMX plumbing from live validation. Can move earlier if a user needs it.

docs.title: Phase 4: Reach
docs.text:
Features that widen who can use the library. They come last because each one touches every widget, so doing them after phases 2 and 3 means less retrofitting.

# Item Status Why in this order 18 #235 Build a FormModel from JSON Schema Not started The library-sized answer to #190. Close #190 when this ships. With FormBuilder removed (#255), this is the friendly way to build a form at runtime; until it ships, the create_model(..., __base__=FormModel) recipe in docs/advanced/runtime-forms.md covers it. 19 #240 Internationalization Not started Wraps every library-generated string and display format. Doing it after the new widgets and display mode means doing it once. 20 #266 Review other UI frameworks Not started Research only: pick which styles to add (for example Tailwind/daisyUI, Bulma, Pico) against criteria such as maintenance, licence and asset size. Feeds #247, so do it first. Adding a style is cheap only after #265 puts every style on one rendering path. 21 #247 CSS-variables theme and the Materialize decision Not started A new style multiplies the work for every widget, so add it once the widget set has settled and #265 has put every style on one rendering path. The Materialize question is settled by #265: the Material style already uses its own embedded theme, not Materialize. 22 #244 Litestar and Django adapters Not started Independent of everything above and can be picked up any time, for example by an outside contributor.

docs.title: Parked
docs.text: Item Why parked #147 Replace MkDocs Material Waiting on Zensical to leave alpha; migrate spring 2027, before MkDocs Material's end of life on 2027-05-05. Research is done: Zensical builds our mkdocs.yml as-is (tested), and a non-blocking CI job builds the docs with it on every PR. Docs aren't part of the package, so this doesn't hold up a release. #251 Dynamic step wizard (steps built from earlier answers, such as a car or product configurator or a BOM builder) A complex addition that needs design before it's scheduled, and it's out of scope for the current wizard work. Revisit after #237, #238, #239 and #250 have shipped. It probably needs a wizard mode where the server keeps state between steps. #236 Form versioning with a migration chain Wait until a real user asks. The library doesn't store data, so most of the value comes from a documented recipe.

docs.title: Not planned
docs.text:
• A visual drag-and-drop form builder. It needs persistence, auth and a design surface, which makes it a product, not a library feature. JSON Schema import (#235) is the library's part of #190.
  • Tier 5 inputs from #178. Map pickers, barcode scanners, camera recording, voice input, passkeys and hosted CAPTCHA all need external services or API keys.

docs.title: Testing & Contribution Workflow
docs.text: This document describes the authoritative workflow for running tests, linting, and contributing to pydantic-schemaforms.

docs.title: Single Entry Point: make tests
docs.text:
Use make tests (or make test) as the single, canonical command for running all quality checks before committing:

make tests

This runs: 1. Pre-commit hooks (Ruff linting + formatting, YAML/TOML checks, trailing whitespace) 2. Type check (pyright) 3. Parser regression suite (tests/test_form_data_parsing.py) 4. Full pytest suite (~1,500 tests covering validation, rendering, async, layouts, examples, integration) 5. Coverage badge generation (summarizes test coverage)

docs.title: What Changed
docs.text:
• Ruff is now enabled in .pre-commit-config.yaml and runs as part of make tests
  • Pre-commit hooks are mandatory before pytest runs; if linting fails, tests don't start
  • No manual ruff invocation needed — it's automatic via pre-commit

docs.title: Before Committing
docs.text:
# Full quality check
make tests

# Or run individual steps if debugging:
make ruff          # Lint + format only
make isort         # Sort imports

docs.title: To 26.4.3: one way to build a form
docs.text:
The builder API, the React and Vue adapters and @form_validator are removed. Importing a removed name raises an ImportError that names its replacement.

Removed Replacement FormBuilder, AutoFormBuilder, create_form_from_model A FormModel class. For fields known only at runtime, create_model(..., __base__=FormModel); see Forms Built at Runtime. create_login_form, create_registration_form, create_contact_form The Login and Registration and Contact Form recipes render_form_page, FormIntegration, handle_form, handle_form_async render_form_html(), FormModel.validate() and result.render_with_errors(); see Handling Submissions @form_validator (it never ran) Pydantic's @model_validator(mode="after"), whose message lands in the form-wide "_errors", or FormValidator.add_cross_field_rule() ReactJSONSchemaFormAdapter, VueFormulateAdapter FormModel.get_pydantic_json_schema() or as_api_model(); see JSON API and JSON Schema DataTableLayout inputs named rows[i].col, csv_file The same names under the embedding field: employees.rows[i].col, employees.csv_file. Only code that reads these keys directly changes.

docs.title: To 26.4.1: nested forms
docs.text:
Version 26.4.1 removed the older ways of combining forms. Using any of them raises FormLayoutRemovedError whose message contains these steps.

Removed Replacement TabbedLayout, VerticalLayout, HorizontalLayout wrapper classes Nested FormModel fields plus layout="tabbed" / "vertical" / "side-by-side" ListLayout(Item, ...) items: list[Item] = Field(default_factory=list, title="Items") SectionDesign(section_title=..., ...) Field(title=..., ui_help_text=..., ui_collapsible=True) on the sub-form field FormDesign(...) Arguments to render_form_html(...) and your page template parse_nested_form_data(...) in routes Pass the request form straight to validate() validate(..., flatten=True) Removed; result.data is always nested Error keys like "pets[0].name" result.errors["pets"][0]["name"] errors={"general": ...} errors={"_errors": ...} layout="tabbed" on a flat form (keyword-guessed tabs) Split the form into sub-forms; each becomes a tab Several input_type="layout" fields auto-tabbing layout="tabbed" on the parent

Before:

class ContactTab(VerticalLayout):
    form = Contact


class AddressTab(VerticalLayout):
    form = Address


class ProfileTabs(TabbedLayout):
    contact = ContactTab()
    address = AddressTab()


class ProfileForm(FormModel):
    tabs: ProfileTabs = Field(default_factory=ProfileTabs, input_type='layout')


data = parse_nested_form_data(await request.form())
result = ProfileForm.validate(data, submit_url='/profile')
city_error = result.errors.get('city')

After:

class ProfileForm(FormModel):
    contact: Contact = Field(title='Contact')
    address: Address = Field(title='Address')


html = render_form_html(ProfileForm, layout='tabbed', submit_url='/profile')
result = ProfileForm.validate(await request.form(), submit_url='/profile', layout='tabbed')
city_error = result.errors.get('address', {}).get('city')

Submitted data and saved records change shape too: the contact fields now arrive under data["contact"] instead of at the top level.
