• ui_options={"language": ...} turns a text area into a small code editor: highlighting, Tab to indent, and a Format button. It's still a plain <textarea>, so it works without JavaScript.
  • The languages are json, yaml, toml, bash and python. JSON, YAML and TOML are really reformatted. Bash and Python only get their whitespace cleaned up, and the button says so.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Each sub-form is a step, titled by its field's title, in the order the fields are declared. The repeating experience list is a step of its own.
  • layout="wizard" is passed to validate() too, so a failed submit comes back as a wizard, opened at the first step with an error.
  • Next checks the current step in the browser before moving on, and the server checks everything on submit.
  • wizard_options renames the Next button here; it can also rename Back, hide the progress header or let users jump between steps. See Layouts.
  • The consent box has no default, so it's required: the form can't be sent without it.

Since no state is kept between steps, there is nothing to store in a session, and the browser's back button and a page reload behave like on any form.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Complete lists of what the library offers, for looking things up. To learn the library, start with the Tutorial.

  • Input Types: every ui_element and its options.
  • Layouts: the layout= values, wizard options and sub-form options.
  • Field Options: everything Field() accepts.
  • Validation Rules: FormValidator, the rule classes and LiveValidator.
  • Rendering API: render_form_html(), FormModel, ValidationResult and html().
  • Accessibility: what every form does for screen readers and keyboards, and how it's tested.

Everything listed here is imported from the top-level package, from pydantic_schemaforms import .... Anything you'd have to import from a submodule is internal and may change without notice.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Accessible forms are part of what this library ships, not an add-on: every release is tested with axe-core, the accessibility engine behind many enterprise audit tools, and a release can't pass CI with a serious or critical violation on any example page.

Testing, not a compliance claim

pydantic-schemaforms does not claim ADA, Section 508, EN 301 549 or WCAG conformance. Conformance is a property of your whole application (page layout, content, navigation, your own CSS) and needs manual review with assistive technology as well as automated tools. What this library gives you is form markup that is automatically tested against the WCAG A and AA rules axe can check, so the forms are a sound starting point for your own audit.

docs.title: What is tested
docs.text:
Aspect Detail Engine axe-core 4.14.0, pinned by version and SHA-256 Rule sets WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 at levels A and AA, plus axe's best-practice rules. axe maps the same rules to Section 508 and EN 301 549. Fails the build on Any violation axe rates serious or critical Pages Every page of the example app, which renders every input type, widget option, layout and composite control the library supports Styles Bootstrap and Material States The initial form and the error state after a failed submit (messages, aria-invalid, the error summary) When On every pull request, in the Playwright CI job

The test lives in tests/playwright/test_example_pages.py. Run it locally with:

playwright install chromium
pytest tests/playwright/test_example_pages.py -k accessibility --no-cov -p no:xdist

docs.title: What the library guarantees
docs.text:
Every built-in input meets this baseline under Bootstrap, Material and plain HTML:

  • Every control has an accessible name. A field's title becomes its <label for=...>; radio and checkbox groups use a <fieldset> with a <legend>. Controls without a visible label of their own, such as DataTableLayout cells, carry an aria-label ("Email, row 3").
  • Help and errors are announced with the field. The control's aria-describedby points at its help text (<id>-help) and, after a failed submit, its error message (<id>-error), and the control gets aria-invalid="true".
  • Text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) in the default themes, including the tags input and the code editor's syntax colors.
  • Click targets are at least 24×24 px (WCAG 2.2 target size), including icon buttons such as the date picker toggle.
  • Decorative layers stay out of the way. Visual-only elements, such as the code editor's syntax-highlight layer, are aria-hidden and never take keyboard focus.

docs.title: What automated testing does not cover
docs.text:
Automated tools find only part of what a full WCAG audit covers. These are not checked by the gate and are worth reviewing by hand in your application:

  • Keyboard flow through multi-step and grouped layouts (wizard, tabs, accordion): focus order and where focus lands after a step change.
  • Screen reader announcements of live (HTMX) validation as the user types.
  • Your own page: the template, headings, landmarks, navigation and any colors or CSS you add around the form.
  • Content: whether labels, help text and error messages are clear.
  • Moderate and minor axe findings, which the gate reports to axe but does not fail on.

docs.title: Keeping your app accessible
docs.text:
• Give every field a title (or rely on the generated one from the field name); it becomes the label. Don't hide labels with CSS without giving the control another name.
  • Keep the library's ARIA attributes when post-processing rendered HTML.
  • Run axe-core against your own pages in your end-to-end tests. The pattern in tests/playwright/test_example_pages.py (inject axe.min.js, call axe.run(), fail on serious or critical violations) works in any Playwright suite.
  • Custom inputs registered with register_input_class should follow the rules in Plugin Hooks so they keep the same baseline.

Found an accessibility problem in a built-in input or layout? Please open an issue; it is treated as a bug.

docs.title: Field Options
docs.text: pydantic_schemaforms.Field() takes everything Pydantic's Field() takes, plus the form settings below. The form settings only change how a field is rendered; validation comes from the type and the Pydantic constraints.

docs.title: Label and help
docs.text: Option Effect title="..." The label. Without it, the field name is used: team_size becomes "Team Size". description="..." Help text under the input. Also appears in the JSON Schema. ui_help_text="..." Help text for the form only; shown instead of description ui_placeholder="..." Grey hint text inside an empty input

docs.title: Choosing the input
docs.text: Option Effect ui_element="..." The input to render, such as "textarea", "radio" or "currency". Without it, the input comes from the field's type. See Input Types. input_type="..." Same as ui_element. ui_options={...} Settings for that input, such as rows, choices or language. Keys an input doesn't use become HTML attributes on it, for example {"autocomplete": "username"}.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text: Option Effect ui_autofocus=True The cursor starts in this field ui_disabled=True The input is greyed out. Browsers don't submit disabled inputs, so the field gets its default when validated. ui_readonly=True The input can't be changed but is submitted ui_hidden=True Rendered as <input type="hidden">, same as ui_element="hidden" ui_order=n Position among the fields (lower first); fields otherwise follow declaration order ui_class="..." Extra CSS classes on the input ui_style="..." Inline CSS on the input

docs.title: Sub-forms and lists
docs.text:
Options on a field typed as a FormModel or a list of one, described in Layouts:

  • Sub-form: ui_collapsible, ui_collapsed, ui_step_title, ui_order.
  • Repeating sub-form: ui_add_button_label, ui_item_title_template, ui_collapsible_items, ui_items_expanded.

Composite controls registered through Plugin Hooks use input_type="layout" with layout_handler="...".

docs.title: Pydantic options
docs.text:
Any Pydantic Field() option works as usual. The ones that matter to forms:

Option In the form default, default_factory The value a fresh form starts with. A field without one is required and its label gets *. min_length, max_length Checked on submit; minlength/maxlength attributes on text inputs. On a list, the fewest and most items. ge, le Checked on submit; min/max attributes on number inputs gt, lt Checked on submit only multiple_of Checked on submit; step attribute on number inputs (a float field otherwise gets step="any") pattern Checked on submit; pattern attribute on text inputs alias The input is named after the alias, and result.data uses the field name examples Shown in the JSON Schema and in FastAPI's API docs, not in the form validate_default=True Runs validators on a default too, for example to require a ticked checkbox with a custom message

A constraint that must hold always goes here, not in ui_options: only these are checked on the server.

docs.title: Input Types
docs.text:
Every input the library can render, with its options. The Tutorial explains how an input is chosen: from the field's type, or with ui_element.

Set an input and its options on the field:

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel


class Example(FormModel):
    bio: str = Field("", ui_element="textarea", ui_options={"rows": 6})

ui_options only changes how the input looks and behaves in the browser. A limit that must hold, such as a minimum length or a numeric range, belongs in a Pydantic constraint (min_length, ge, ...): those are checked on the server and also become HTML attributes. Putting the same value in ui_options only decorates the HTML. For a numeric select or radio with explicit choices, keep the choices and ge/le in step, or a choice can render that then fails validation.

Every built-in input is tested with axe-core against the WCAG 2.0–2.2 A and AA rules; see Accessibility.

docs.title: Every input type
docs.text: Every registered ui_element, generated from examples/input_type_reference.py (the same data backing the FastAPI demo's /input-types page). Run python scripts/generate_input_type_reference.py after changing that file to regenerate this section.

docs.title: Text Inputs
docs.text:
text — Single-line free text. The default when no ui_element is given. 

name: str = Field(..., ui_element='text', ui_placeholder='Full name')

textarea — Multi-line free text. Add language= for a Format button, Tab-key indentation, and syntax highlighting (json/yaml/toml/bash/python). 

bio: str = Field('', ui_element='textarea', ui_options={'rows': 4})
config: str = Field('{}', ui_element='textarea',
                    ui_options={'language': 'json', 'rows': 8})

email — Email input with built-in browser validation and a numeric-friendly mobile keyboard. 

email: str = Field(..., ui_element='email', ui_placeholder='you@example.com')

password — Password input; autocomplete defaults to 'new-password' so browsers don't offer to autofill a saved password. 

password: str = Field(..., ui_element='password')

search — Search input with a search-oriented mobile keyboard. 

query: str = Field('', ui_element='search', ui_placeholder='Search...')

url — URL input with browser validation and a default http(s):// pattern. 

website: str = Field('', ui_element='url', ui_placeholder='https://example.com')

tel — Plain telephone input, no formatting applied. 

phone: str = Field('', ui_element='tel')

phone (also accepts: phone_number) — Telephone input with a live-formatting mask as the user types. 

phone: str = Field('', ui_element='phone',
                   ui_options={'phone_format': '(###) ###-####'})

ssn (also accepts: social_security_number) — Social Security Number input, formatted 123-45-6789 with a numeric keyboard. 

ssn: str = Field('', ui_element='ssn')

credit_card (also accepts: card, cc_number) — Credit card number input, grouped 1234 5678 9012 3456. 

card_number: str = Field('', ui_element='credit_card')

currency (also accepts: money) — Currency input with live thousands-separator formatting as the user types. 

price: str = Field('', ui_element='currency',
                   ui_options={'currency_symbol': '$'})

docs.title: Numeric Inputs
docs.text:
number — Plain HTML number input. 

count: int = Field(0, ui_element='number')

integer — Number input constrained to whole numbers (step=1). 

quantity: int = Field(1, ui_element='integer')

decimal — Number input with a configurable decimal precision (sets step from it). 

price: float = Field(0.0, ui_element='decimal',
                     ui_options={'decimal_places': 2})

percentage — Number input clamped to 0-100 by default. 

discount: float = Field(0, ui_element='percentage')

age — Integer input with sensible age bounds (0-150) pre-filled. 

age: int = Field(..., ui_element='age')

quantity — Integer input for carts/inventory: min=1, placeholder '1'. 

qty: int = Field(1, ui_element='quantity')

score — Number input with a configurable min/max range (default 0-100). 

score: float = Field(0, ui_element='score',
                     ui_options={'min_score': 0, 'max_score': 10})

range — Native HTML range slider. 

volume: int = Field(50, ui_element='range', ge=0, le=100)

slider — Range slider with min/max value labels shown alongside it. 

opacity: int = Field(100, ui_element='slider', ge=0, le=100)

rating (also accepts: rating_stars) — Range slider styled to show a 1-N star rating (default max 5). 

rating: int = Field(3, ui_element='rating', ui_options={'max_rating': 5})

temperature — Number input whose placeholder and absolute-zero minimum follow unit (celsius/fahrenheit/kelvin). 

temp: float = Field(20.0, ui_element='temperature',
                    ui_options={'unit': 'celsius'})

docs.title: Date/Time Inputs
docs.text:
date — Native HTML date picker (YYYY-MM-DD). 

birth_date: date = Field(..., ui_element='date')

time — Native HTML time picker. 

appt_time: time = Field(..., ui_element='time')

datetime (also accepts: datetime-local) — Native HTML datetime-local picker. 

starts_at: datetime = Field(..., ui_element='datetime')

month — Native HTML month picker (YYYY-MM). 

billing_month: str = Field(..., ui_element='month')

week — Native HTML week picker (YYYY-Www). 

sprint_week: str = Field(..., ui_element='week')

birthdate — Date input pre-configured with sane birthdate bounds. 

dob: date = Field(..., ui_element='birthdate')

docs.title: Selection Inputs
docs.text:
checkbox — Single boolean checkbox. 

agree: bool = Field(False, ui_element='checkbox', title='I accept the terms')

toggle (also accepts: toggle_switch, checkbox_toggle) — Single boolean rendered as a modern switch instead of a checkbox. 

enabled: bool = Field(True, ui_element='toggle')

checkbox_group — Multiple booleans from one field, rendered as a group of checkboxes. ui_options collapsible=True turns the legend into a toggle that shows/hides the options -- purely presentational, does not affect required-ness. 

channels: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, ui_element='checkbox_group',
                            ui_options={'choices': ['email', 'sms', 'push'],
                                        'collapsible': True})

radio — Single choice from a set of mutually-exclusive options. Also supports ui_options collapsible/collapsed, same as checkbox_group. 

size: str = Field('medium', ui_element='radio',
                  ui_options={'choices': ['small', 'medium', 'large']})

select — Native HTML dropdown, single choice. ui_options placeholder= renders a disabled blank option forcing a real selection, instead of the browser defaulting to the first option. 

plan: str = Field(..., ui_element='select',
                  ui_options={'placeholder': 'Choose a plan...', 'choices': [
                      {'value': 'free', 'label': 'Free'},
                      {'value': 'pro', 'label': 'Pro'},
                  ]})

multiselect — Multi-choice dropdown, enhanced with a searchable chips UI over the real . 

tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, ui_element='multiselect',
                        ui_options={'options': [
                            {'value': 'py', 'label': 'Python'},
                            {'value': 'rs', 'label': 'Rust'},
                        ]})

combobox — Text input with a suggestion dropdown (native ) -- free text is still allowed, unlike select. 

city: str = Field('', ui_element='combobox',
                  ui_options={'choices': ['New York', 'London', 'Tokyo']})

docs.title: Files & Specialized Inputs
docs.text:
file — File upload input. 

files: str = Field(..., ui_element='file',
                   ui_options={'accept': '.pdf,.docx', 'multiple': True})

color — Native HTML color picker. 

theme_color: str = Field('#3498db', ui_element='color')

hidden — Hidden input, not shown to the user but submitted with the form. 

session_id: str = Field(..., ui_element='hidden')

tags — Chip/tag entry: press Enter or comma to add a tag, Backspace to remove the last one; a hidden input carries the joined value. 

keywords: str = Field('', ui_element='tags',
                      ui_help_text='Press Enter or comma to add a tag')

star_rating — Individually clickable stars (contrast with rating, which is a slider). 

stars: int = Field(0, ui_element='star_rating', ui_options={'max_stars': 5})

captcha — Simple math-challenge CAPTCHA for spam resistance without a third-party service. 

captcha: str = Field('', ui_element='captcha')

honeypot — Invisible trap field for bots -- real users never see or fill it; a filled honeypot means reject the submission. 

website_url: str = Field('', ui_element='honeypot')

csrf — Hidden CSRF token field -- typically added by the framework integration, not hand-declared per form. 

csrf_token: str = Field(..., ui_element='csrf')

docs.title: Options by input
docs.text:
Each input lists what it needs and the ui_options it accepts. The examples assume:

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
• text (default)
  • password
  • email
  • search
  • textarea
  • url
  • tel

docs.title: text
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="text"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: minlength, maxlength, pattern, autocomplete, inputmode
class TextExample(FormModel):
    username: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="text",
        ui_placeholder="jane_doe",
        ui_options={"minlength": 3, "maxlength": 32, "autocomplete": "username"},
    )

docs.title: password
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="password"

Optional:

  • ui_options: minlength, maxlength, autocomplete (defaults to new-password)
class PasswordExample(FormModel):
    password: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="password",
        ui_placeholder="Enter a strong password",
        ui_options={"minlength": 12, "autocomplete": "new-password"},
    )

docs.title: email
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="email"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: autocomplete, pattern, maxlength
class EmailExample(FormModel):
    email: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="email",
        ui_placeholder="name@company.com",
        ui_options={"autocomplete": "email", "maxlength": 254},
    )

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="search"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: maxlength, autocomplete
class SearchExample(FormModel):
    q: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="search",
        ui_placeholder="Search products",
        ui_options={"maxlength": 120, "autocomplete": "off"},
    )

docs.title: textarea
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="textarea"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: rows, cols, wrap, resize, minlength, maxlength
class TextAreaExample(FormModel):
    bio: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="textarea",
        ui_placeholder="Tell us about yourself",
        ui_options={"rows": 5, "cols": 60, "wrap": "soft", "resize": "vertical"},
    )

docs.title: url
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="url"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: pattern, autocomplete
class UrlExample(FormModel):
    website: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="url",
        ui_placeholder="https://example.com",
        ui_options={"pattern": r"https?://.+", "autocomplete": "url"},
    )

docs.title: tel
docs.text:
Required:

  • Field type + ui_element="tel"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: pattern, autocomplete, maxlength
class TelExample(FormModel):
    phone: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="tel",
        ui_placeholder="+1 555 123 4567",
        ui_options={"autocomplete": "tel", "maxlength": 20},
    )

Notes:

  • Long string fields may auto-infer to textarea.
  • password preserves the value if you supply one (use with care).

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• number
  • range
  • percentage, decimal, integer, age, quantity, score, temperature (see Specialized numeric elements)
  • rating (alias: rating_stars), star_rating, slider (see Rating & sliders)

docs.title: number
docs.text:
Required:

  • Numeric field type + ui_element="number"

Optional:

  • Pydantic constraints: ge, le, gt, lt, multiple_of
  • ui_options: min, max, step, inputmode, show_stepper
class NumberExample(FormModel):
    quantity: int = Field(
        ...,
        ge=1,
        le=100,
        ui_element="number",
        ui_options={"step": 1, "inputmode": "numeric"},
    )

Set ui_options={"show_stepper": True} to render +/- buttons on either side of the input instead of relying on the browser's native number spinner. The buttons dispatch real input/change events, so they work with any other JS listening on the field. quantity (below) turns this on by default.

docs.title: range
docs.text:
Required:

  • Numeric field type + ui_element="range"

Optional:

  • ui_options: min, max, step, value, show_value
class RangeExample(FormModel):
    satisfaction: int = Field(
        ...,
        ge=0,
        le=10,
        ui_element="range",
        ui_options={"min": 0, "max": 10, "step": 1, "value": 7, "show_value": True},
    )

docs.title: Specialized numeric elements
docs.text:
These all build on number and accept the same ui_options (min, max, step, show_stepper) plus their own defaults/kwargs listed below.

ui_element Purpose Extra ui_options percentage Adds a % placeholder, defaults min/max/step to 0-100/0.1 -- decimal Step derived from decimal_places decimal_places (int, default 2) integer Forces step=1, numeric keyboard -- age Integer with min/max defaulted to 0-150 -- quantity Integer with min=1 and show_stepper=True by default -- score Free min/max range (defaults 0-100) min_score, max_score temperature Unit-aware placeholder/min/max unit ("celsius" | "fahrenheit" | "kelvin") 
class SpecializedNumericExample(FormModel):
    discount: float = Field(..., ui_element="percentage")
    price: float = Field(..., ui_element="decimal", ui_options={"decimal_places": 2})
    attendees: int = Field(..., ui_element="integer")
    applicant_age: int = Field(..., ui_element="age")
    cart_quantity: int = Field(1, ui_element="quantity")  # ships the +/- stepper by default
    exam_score: float = Field(..., ui_element="score", ui_options={"min_score": 0, "max_score": 100})
    room_temp: float = Field(..., ui_element="temperature", ui_options={"unit": "fahrenheit"})

docs.title: Rating & sliders
docs.text:
• rating (alias: rating_stars): a range slider that also renders a live ★★★☆☆-style text readout. Accepts ui_options={"max_rating": 5} (defaults to 5). Good for a compact, keyboard/touch-friendly rating input.
  • star_rating: individually clickable stars (not a slider) -- contrast with rating above. Accepts ui_options={"max_stars": 5} (note the different option name from rating's max_rating).
  • slider: range with min/max value labels shown below the track. Accepts ui_options={"show_labels": True} (default) plus the usual min/max/step.
class RatingAndSliderExample(FormModel):
    satisfaction: int = Field(3, ui_element="rating", ui_options={"max_rating": 5})
    quality_stars: int = Field(4, ui_element="star_rating", ui_options={"max_stars": 5})
    volume: int = Field(50, ui_element="slider", ui_options={"min": 0, "max": 100, "step": 5})

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
• select
  • multiselect
  • checkbox
  • checkbox_group
  • radio
  • toggle (aliases: toggle_switch, checkbox_toggle)
  • combobox

Literal[...] auto-populates options; a real enum.Enum/StrEnum does not — this applies to every widget below that reads "schema enum" as a way to provide choices (select, radio, checkbox_group, multiselect, combobox). Pydantic inlines a Literal[...] field's values directly into that field's own JSON schema entry, which is what these widgets read to build their options; for an actual Enum class, Pydantic instead points the field at a separate $defs entry via $ref, which none of these widgets resolve. The failure mode isn't a wrong label — it's a silently empty control (a <select> with no <option>s, an HTML comment where the options should be) that's easy to miss in review. Always pass ui_options={"choices": [e.value for e in MyEnum]} explicitly for a real Enum field. If nothing requires pinning specific literal string values in the type itself, prefer Literal[...] over Enum to avoid this entirely.

docs.title: select
docs.text:
Required:

  • ui_element="select"
  • ui_options with choices/options list, or schema enum

Optional:

  • ui_options: options, choices, size, class, style, placeholder
class SelectExample(FormModel):
    region: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="select",
        ui_options={
            "options": [
                {"value": "na", "label": "North America"},
                {"value": "eu", "label": "Europe"},
            ],
            "size": 1,
        },
    )

ui_options={"placeholder": "..."} renders a disabled, empty-value first option forcing a genuine choice, instead of the browser silently highlighting the first real option as if it were already picked:

class PlanExample(FormModel):
    plan: str = Field(
        ...,
        title="Plan",
        ui_element="select",
        ui_options={"choices": ["free", "pro", "enterprise"], "placeholder": "Choose a plan..."},
    )

The placeholder option is only ever the initially-shown, selected one when nothing has been chosen yet -- once a real value is set (a default, a previous submission, a validation-error re-render), the placeholder stays in the list but loses selected and remains disabled, so it can't be picked again. Combined with the required attribute this library already adds for required fields, native browser validation blocks submission until a real option is chosen -- no extra server-side validation needed for Enum/Literal-backed or min_length-constrained fields, since an empty string already fails those. Works identically on bootstrap/plain/none and material frameworks.

docs.title: multiselect
docs.text:
Required:

  • ui_element="multiselect"
  • ui_options with choices/options list, or schema enum

Optional:

  • ui_options: options, choices, size, enhanced (default True), searchable (default True), search_placeholder
class MultiSelectExample(FormModel):
    tags: list[str] = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="multiselect",
        ui_options={
            "options": [
                {"value": "backend", "label": "Backend"},
                {"value": "frontend", "label": "Frontend"},
                {"value": "infra", "label": "Infra"},
            ],
            "size": 4,
        },
    )

The real <select multiple> is always rendered -- it's what the form actually submits, JS or not. By default (enhanced=True) it's layered with a chips + search UI that reads its option data straight off the <select>, and only hides the native control once the enhanced UI has built successfully, so a JS load failure never leaves the field invisible. Set ui_options={"enhanced": False} to render the plain native multi-select instead, or ui_options={"searchable": False} to keep the chips UI without the search box.

docs.title: checkbox
docs.text:
Required:

  • bool field type + ui_element="checkbox"

Optional:

  • ui_options: value, checked, label
class CheckboxExample(FormModel):
    terms_accepted: bool = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="checkbox",
        ui_help_text="I agree to the terms and privacy policy",
        ui_options={"value": "1", "checked": False},
    )

docs.title: checkbox_group
docs.text:
Required:

  • list field type + ui_element="checkbox_group"
  • ui_options with choices/options list, or schema enum

Optional:

  • ui_options: options, choices, legend, variant ("stacked" default, or "button_group"), collapsible, collapsed
class CheckboxGroupExample(FormModel):
    notify_via: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        ui_element="checkbox_group",
        ui_options={
            "choices": [
                {"value": "email", "label": "Email"},
                {"value": "sms", "label": "SMS"},
                {"value": "push", "label": "Push"},
            ],
            "legend": "Notify me via",
        },
    )

Use this instead of multiselect when you want independent on/off checkboxes laid out directly on the page rather than a dropdown -- both submit a list of selected values. variant="button_group" adds checkbox-group-button-group/checkbox-item-button-group modifier classes for styling the options as an adjacent button row; it's presentation only, your app's CSS still does the actual visual styling (removing borders between items, etc.).

ui_options={"collapsible": True} turns the legend into a clickable toggle that shows/hides the checkboxes underneath -- useful for grouping a long options list (e.g. a "Vegetables"/"Condiments"/"Extra" set of toppings) so it doesn't take up space until opened. collapsed=True starts it closed (default: open). Purely presentational, like variant -- it never changes which fields are required; that's still driven entirely by the field's own Field(...) declaration.

docs.title: radio
docs.text:
Required:

  • ui_element="radio"
  • ui_options with choices/options list, or schema enum

Optional:

  • ui_options: options, choices, legend, variant ("stacked" default, or "segmented"), class, style, collapsible, collapsed
class RadioExample(FormModel):
    plan: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="radio",
        ui_options={
            "choices": [
                {"value": "free", "label": "Free"},
                {"value": "pro", "label": "Pro"},
            ],
            "legend": "Subscription plan",
        },
    )

variant="segmented" adds radio-group-segmented/radio-item-segmented modifier classes for styling the options as adjacent buttons instead of stacked radios -- presentation only, same caveat as checkbox_group's button_group variant above.

ui_options={"collapsible": True} (and collapsed=True to start closed) works identically to checkbox_group's -- see above.

docs.title: toggle (aliases: toggle_switch, checkbox_toggle)
docs.text:
Required:

  • bool field type + ui_element="toggle"

Optional:

  • ui_options: label, checked, class
class ToggleExample(FormModel):
    marketing_opt_in: bool = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="toggle",
        ui_options={"label": "Receive product updates", "checked": True},
    )

docs.title: combobox
docs.text:
Required:

  • ui_element="combobox"
  • ui_options with choices/options list, or schema enum

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: options, choices, filter_mode ("contains" default, or "startswith"), min_chars
class ComboBoxExample(FormModel):
    city: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="combobox",
        ui_placeholder="Select or type a city",
        ui_options={
            "options": [
                {"value": "nyc", "label": "New York"},
                {"value": "ldn", "label": "London"},
                {"value": "tky", "label": "Tokyo"},
            ]
        },
    )

Renders a text input backed by a native <datalist> (the no-JS fallback) plus a JS-filtered dropdown listbox with arrow-key navigation and click-to-select, built from the same option data as the datalist -- nothing to keep in sync. filter_mode="startswith" restricts matches to the beginning of each option's label instead of matching anywhere in it.

Selection note:

  • Provide choices via ui_options={"options": [...]} or ui_options={"choices": [...]}.
  • Or use a Literal[...]-typed field and options are inferred (a real Enum is not inferred this way -- see the note at the top of this "Selection" section).

docs.title: Date/time
docs.text:
• date
  • time
  • datetime (alias: datetime-local)
  • month
  • week
  • birthdate

docs.title: date
docs.text:
Required:

  • date-like field + ui_element="date"

Optional:

  • ui_options: min, max, value, date_format
from datetime import date


class DateExample(FormModel):
    start_date: date = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="date",
        ui_options={"min": date(2026, 1, 1), "max": date(2026, 12, 31)},
    )

Set ui_options={"date_format": "%d/%m/%Y"} to display and submit the field in a custom shape using standard strftime/strptime directives, instead of the browser's own locale-controlled date picker. This renders as a live-formatted text input (native <input type="date"> can't show a custom display format -- the browser always controls it). Without date_format, the field renders exactly as before. The server still parses and validates the submitted value; a plain ISO YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g. from a JSON API caller bypassing the HTML form) is still accepted regardless of the configured display format. BirthdateInput (ui_element="birthdate") inherits date_format support the same way.

A custom-format field stays a single visible box (live_format=True, the default). Two independent capabilities layer on top of it:

  • Picker icon button: for any format built from directives a JS Date object can supply a value for (%Y %y %m %d %H %I %M %S %p %B %b %A %a), a small calendar icon button appears inside the field -- clicking it calls the browser's native showPicker() on a visually-hidden, non-submitting companion <input type="date"> behind the scenes, and selecting a date writes it into the visible field already converted to the custom format (including AM/PM and month/weekday names, via a hardcoded English name table). Only truly exotic directives (%Z, %j, %f, week numbers, ...) omit the icon entirely.
  • Live per-character typing mask: for formats built entirely from fixed-width numeric directives (%Y %y %m %d %H %I %M %S), digits are auto-punctuated as the user types. Formats using a variable-width directive (%p, weekday/month names, ...) don't get this -- there's no safe way to live-mask "AM"/"PM" or a month name character by character -- but the picker icon above still works for them.

docs.title: time
docs.text:
Required:

  • time-like field + ui_element="time"

Optional:

  • ui_options: min, max, step, value, time_format
from datetime import time


class TimeExample(FormModel):
    start_time: time = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="time",
        ui_options={"min": time(9, 0), "max": time(18, 0), "step": 900},
    )

Set ui_options={"time_format": "%H:%M"} for 24-hour ("military") time, or any other strftime shape -- same mechanism as date_format above (falls back to a live-formatted text input with a picker icon button; native <input type="time"> can't be forced into a custom display format). step only applies to the native time picker and is not used once a custom time_format is set.

docs.title: datetime (alias: datetime-local)
docs.text:
Required:

  • datetime-like field + ui_element="datetime"

Optional:

  • ui_options: min, max, value, auto_set_current, with_set_now_button, datetime_format
from datetime import datetime


class DatetimeExample(FormModel):
    appointment_at: datetime = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="datetime",
        ui_options={"auto_set_current": True, "with_set_now_button": True},
    )

Set ui_options={"datetime_format": "%Y%m%d%H%M%S"} for an arbitrary custom shape (e.g. year-month-day-hour(24)-minute-second) -- same mechanism as date_format/time_format, including the picker icon button (also available for %p/%B/etc., see above). When both datetime_format and with_set_now_button are set, the Set Now button writes a value matching the custom format instead of the default ISO-ish shape, using the same JS-Date-derivable directive set as the picker icon -- omitted entirely only for the rarer directives that set omits too (%Z, %j, %f, ...).

Known limitation: the standalone FieldValidator(...).date_range() rule (as opposed to ui_options={"min": ..., "max": ...} above) always expects ISO YYYY-MM-DD values and is not aware of date_format/ time_format/datetime_format. Use the min/max ui_options shown above for range constraints on a custom-formatted field -- they're already format-aware.

See examples/date_time_formats_example.py for a live-runnable showcase of 21 date/time/datetime formats (USA, Europe, Asia, military time, and compact year-month-day-hour-minute-second shapes) across all three input types, wired up at the /date-time-formats route in the FastAPI example app.

docs.text:
Required:

  • date/datetime/string field + ui_element="month"

Optional:

  • ui_options: min, max, value (YYYY-MM)
class MonthExample(FormModel):
    billing_month: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="month",
        ui_options={"min": "2026-01", "max": "2026-12", "value": "2026-04"},

class WeekExample(FormModel):

docs.title: birthdate
docs.text:
Required:

  • date-like field + ui_element="birthdate"

Optional:

  • ui_options: min, max (defaults to today and 150 years ago), show_age (default True)
from datetime import date


class BirthdateExample(FormModel):
    date_of_birth: date = Field(..., ui_element="birthdate")

show_age renders a live "You are N years old" readout below the field, computed client-side and updated as the date changes. Set ui_options={"show_age": False} to render a plain date input with birthdate-appropriate min/max defaults but no age display.

docs.text:
• file

docs.title: file
docs.text:
Required:

  • Any-typed field + ui_element="file" (the upload arrives as your framework's file object; see the File Upload recipe)

Optional:

  • ui_options: accept, multiple, capture, show_preview, enable_drag_drop (default True)
from typing import Any


class FileExample(FormModel):
    attachments: Any = Field(
        None,
        ui_element="file",
        ui_options={
            "accept": ".pdf,.docx,image/*",
            "multiple": True,
            "show_preview": True,
        },
    )

Drag-and-drop is on by default: the input renders inside a drop zone that accepts dragged files and feeds them into the same change/preview handling as a click-selected file, so no extra wiring is needed. Set ui_options={"enable_drag_drop": False} to render a plain file input.

docs.text:

Optional:

class ColorExample(FormModel):
    accent_color: str = Field(
        "#0EA5E9",
        ui_element="color",
        ui_options={"show_value": True},

docs.text:
Required:

Optional:

class HiddenExample(FormModel):
    account_id: str = Field(
        "acct_123",
        ui_element="hidden",

docs.text:
Required:

  • string field + ui_element="ssn"

Optional:

class SsnExample(FormModel):
    ssn: str = Field(

        ui_element="ssn",

docs.title: phone (alias: phone_number)
docs.text:
Required:

  • string field + ui_element="phone"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder
  • ui_options: country_code, autocomplete, phone_format, live_format (default True)
class PhoneExample(FormModel):
    contact_phone: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="phone",
        ui_placeholder="555 123 4567",
        ui_options={"country_code": "+1", "autocomplete": "tel"},
    )

Set ui_options={"phone_format": "(###) ###-####"} to get a live-formatting mask -- # marks each digit position, and any other character is inserted literally as the user types. Without phone_format, the field renders exactly as before (no mask). This is display formatting only; it is not a substitute for server-side validation of the submitted value.

docs.title: credit_card (aliases: card, cc_number)
docs.text:
Required:

  • string field + ui_element="credit_card"

Optional:

  • ui_placeholder override
class CreditCardExample(FormModel):
    card_number: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="credit_card",

docs.title: currency (alias: money)
docs.text:
Required:

  • string/decimal-like field + ui_element="currency"

Optional:

  • ui_options: currency_symbol, live_format (default True)
class CurrencyExample(FormModel):
    budget: str = Field(
        ...,
        ui_element="currency",
        ui_options={"currency_symbol": "$"},
    )

live_format inserts thousands separators as the user types (on by default). Set ui_options={"live_format": False} to disable it. On a Decimal, float or int field, validate() strips the symbol and separators before parsing, so $1,234.50 becomes Decimal("1234.50"); a str field keeps the text as typed.

docs.title: tags
docs.text:
Required:

  • string field + ui_element="tags"

Optional:

  • ui_options: placeholder, separator (default ",")
class TagsExample(FormModel):
    skills: str = Field(
        "",
        title="Skills",
        ui_element="tags",
        ui_options={"placeholder": "Add a skill and press Enter", "separator": ","},
    )

Renders a chip-style tags editor backed by a single hidden input that stores the joined, separator-delimited string -- so the field type stays a plain str, not a list[str]. Typing a separator character or pressing Enter turns the current text into a chip; Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip.

These specialized elements are opt-in and will not override normal text fields. Use them explicitly when you want built-in formatting/pattern behavior.

docs.title: captcha
docs.text:
Required:

  • string field + ui_element="captcha"
  • ui_options with a secret_key
from pydantic_schemaforms import verify_captcha

SECRET = "change-me-and-load-from-your-app-config"


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    captcha_answer: str = Field(
        "",
        title="Verify you are human",
        ui_element="captcha",
        ui_options={"secret_key": SECRET},
    )

captcha renders a small arithmetic question ("What is 4 + 7?") plus a hidden, HMAC-signed challenge token -- the correct sum is never sent to the browser. Verify it at the route level, before model validation, since the token only exists in the raw submitted form data:

form_dict = dict(await request.form())
token = form_dict.pop("captcha_answer_token", None)
if not verify_captcha(token=token, answer=form_dict.get("captcha_answer"), secret_key=SECRET):
    # re-render with a form-level error; a fresh challenge is generated
    # automatically since the widget re-renders on every request
    ...

Only declare the visible answer field on your model -- do not also declare a separate ..._token field for it. A new question/token pair is generated on every render, so the token in the page always matches the question shown.

docs.title: honeypot
docs.text:
Required:

  • string field + ui_element="honeypot"
class SignupForm(FormModel):
    website_url: str = Field("", ui_element="honeypot")

Renders a field that is hidden from real users (display: none, tabindex="-1") but still visible to bots that fill in every input they find. If the submitted value is non-empty, treat the submission as spam -- most apps fake a success response rather than revealing that a trap caught it:

if form_dict.get("website_url"):
    return success_response()  # pretend it worked; don't process the submission

docs.title: csrf
docs.text: csrf is rendered by the library's own CSRF handling rather than declared directly as a model field -- pass csrf_mode="required-provider" (or "field-only" for local debugging) and a csrf_token_provider to render_form_html()/render_form_from_model(). See CSRF Protection for the full guide, including how tokens are generated, stored, and verified.

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
• datetime-local is an alias for datetime
  • toggle_switch and checkbox_toggle are aliases for toggle
  • social_security_number is an alias for ssn
  • phone_number is an alias for phone
  • card and cc_number are aliases for credit_card
  • money is an alias for currency
  • rating_stars is an alias for rating (the slider-based widget -- not the same as the separate star_rating element, which is clickable stars)

docs.title: Special elements
docs.text:
These are rendered by the layout engine, not as a single input:

  • model_list: a repeating sub-form, inferred from a list of a FormModel; see Nested Forms and Lists.
  • nested_model: a sub-form, inferred from a field typed as a FormModel.
  • layout: a field rendered by a registered composite renderer, such as Data Tables.

docs.title: Unknown elements
docs.text: An unknown ui_element falls back to a plain text input. To add your own input, subclass an existing one and register it; see Plugin Hooks and Custom Composites.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text: The values of layout= and their options. The Layouts chapter of the tutorial introduces them with a complete example.

docs.title: layout=
docs.text:
Pass layout= to render_form_html() (or render_form_html_async(), FormModel.render_form()) and to FormModel.validate(), so render_with_errors() comes back the same way.

Value What you get "vertical" (default) The form's own fields first, then each sub-form as a titled section "tabbed" One tab for the form's own fields, then one tab per sub-form "side-by-side" The same groups as columns in one row "accordion" The same groups as collapsible panels, the first one open "wizard" The same groups as steps, one at a time, with Back and Next

An unknown value raises ValueError.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
The grouped layouts (tabbed, side-by-side, accordion, wizard) arrange groups:

  • The first group holds the form's own fields (those that aren't sub-forms). Its title is the model's title, model_config = {"title": "About you"}, or "General" when the model has none. It is left out when there are no such fields.
  • Then one group per sub-form field: a field typed as a FormModel, a list of one, or a composite such as a data table.

A form without any sub-form field has nothing to group, so a grouped layout raises a ValueError asking you to split it into nested models.

After a failed submit, the first tab, panel or step with an error is the one that opens, and the error summary at the top of the form stays visible.

docs.title: Sub-form field options
docs.text:
Set these on the sub-form field:

Option Effect title="..." Section heading, tab label, column heading, panel title or step title ui_step_title="..." Step title under layout="wizard" only, instead of title ui_help_text="..." Help text under the section heading ui_order=n Position among the groups (lower first); groups otherwise follow declaration order ui_collapsible=True Under vertical, render the section as a collapsible panel ui_collapsed=True Start the collapsible section closed; it opens when it contains an error

docs.title: wizard_options=
docs.text:
Pass to render_form_html() and validate() together with layout="wizard":

Key Default Effect linear True Clicking a later step in the progress header checks the steps in between. False lets the header jump to any step. show_progress True False hides the progress header. back_label "Back" Text of the Back button next_label "Next" Text of the Next button

An unknown key raises ValueError.

How the wizard behaves:

  • One form, one POST. Every step is in the same <form> and only hidden in the browser. No state is kept between steps.
  • Next checks the current step with the browser's own validation (required, minlength, min/max, pattern, type="email", ...) and stays put if something fails. Back never checks. Enter in a field moves to the next step instead of submitting.
  • The submit button is on the last step. The server validates everything, including rules the browser can't check.
  • After a failed submit, the first step with an error opens and every step with an error is marked in the progress header.
  • Without JavaScript, every step is shown, stacked under its title, with the submit button at the end.

docs.title: Repeating sub-form options
docs.text:
A list of a FormModel renders as cards with Add and Remove buttons. Set these on the list field:

Option Effect min_length=n / max_length=n Fewest and most items, checked in the browser and on the server. With min_length, an empty list starts with that many blank items. ui_add_button_label="..." Text of the Add button ui_item_title_template="..." Each card's title, filled from the item's fields ("{name}"); {index} is the 1-based position ui_collapsible_items=False Plain cards instead of collapsible ones ui_items_expanded=False Start the cards collapsed

docs.title: Other layout tools
docs.text:
• Layout Primitives: grids, cards and tabs for arranging HTML you've already rendered.
  • Plugin Hooks and Custom Composites: register a renderer for a control of your own.

docs.title: Rendering API
docs.text: The functions and methods that turn a model into HTML and a submission into data. Everything is imported from the top-level package.

docs.title: render_form_html()
docs.text:
render_form_html(Model, form_data=None, errors=None, framework="bootstrap", *, submit_url, ...) -> str

Returns the form as an HTML string: the <form> element with its fields, error summary and submit button, plus the small scripts and styles the form's inputs need. It is a fragment for your page, not a whole page.

Argument Default Effect submit_url required The form's action. Never guessed. form_data None Values to show. None starts from the field defaults; a dict is used as is (see Fields and Inputs). Nested dicts, Enum members and dates are fine. errors None Messages to show, shaped like the data: {"email": "..."}, {"address": {"city": "..."}}, "_errors" for the whole form framework "bootstrap" "bootstrap", "material" or "none"; see Styling layout "vertical" See Layouts wizard_options None See Layouts method "POST" The form's method include_submit_button True False leaves the button out, for a form you submit some other way csrf_mode "off" "required-provider" adds a hidden CSRF field; see CSRF Protection csrf_token_provider None The token, or a function returning it csrf_field_name "csrf_token" Name of the hidden CSRF field include_framework_assets False Add the framework's CSS and JavaScript to the output asset_mode "vendored" With assets included: "vendored" inlines the packaged files, "cdn" links pinned CDN copies self_contained False Shortcut for include_framework_assets=True with inlined files, Bootstrap Icons included; see Assets show_timing False Show how long rendering took under the form debug False Add a debug panel with the schema, data and errors enable_logging False Log rendering at DEBUG level; see Render Timing and Logging include_html_markers True Wrap the output in <!--- Start/End Pydantic-SchemaForms --> comments inject_layout_styles True Add the small stylesheet that makes the form fill its container

Any other keyword becomes an attribute of the <form> tag, for example id="signup" or **{"hx-post": "/signup"}. A form with a file input gets enctype="multipart/form-data" unless you pass your own enctype.

docs.title: render_form_html_async()
docs.text: The same arguments and result as render_form_html(). It renders in a worker thread so an async route doesn't block the event loop. Use it in FastAPI and other async frameworks.

docs.title: FormModel
docs.text:
FormModel is a Pydantic BaseModel with these class methods added:

Method Returns validate(data, *, submit_url=None, framework="bootstrap", **render_options) A ValidationResult. data is the raw request form (await request.form(), request.form) or a nested dict such as a JSON body. Render options (layout=, csrf_mode=, ...) are kept for render_with_errors(). render_form(data=None, errors=None, framework="bootstrap", *, submit_url, **options) The same as render_form_html(Model, ...) as_api_model() A plain Pydantic model with the same fields and validation but without the form settings, for request bodies and response_model; see JSON API and JSON Schema get_pydantic_json_schema(**options) The standard JSON Schema, with sub-forms as $defs; Pydantic's model_json_schema() options pass through get_json_schema() The schema the renderer uses internally, form settings included

The model's own model_config = {"title": "..."} titles the form's first group in the grouped layouts.

docs.title: ValidationResult
docs.text: Member Holds is_valid True when everything passed data The validated values, nested like the model ({} when invalid) instance The validated model object (None when invalid) errors The messages, nested like the data; "_errors" holds form-wide ones error_list() The same errors as a flat list: [{"loc": ["pets", 1, "age"], "msg": "..."}] original_data The submission decoded into nested form, before validation render_with_errors(**options) The form again with the submitted values and the errors, using the options given to validate(). Pass errors= to show a different set, such as these merged with a FormValidator's. render_with_errors_async(**options) The same, off the event loop

docs.title: html() and SafeHTML
docs.text:
html(t"...") builds HTML from a Python 3.14 t-string and escapes every interpolated value. Use it for anything you build around submitted data:

from pydantic_schemaforms import html

name = result.data["name"]
page = html(t"<p>Thanks, {name}!</p>")

It returns a SafeHTML, a str that html() won't escape again, so pieces nest. Wrap a string in SafeHTML(...) only when it's HTML you trust, such as another form you rendered.

docs.title: Lower-level pieces
docs.text:
• EnhancedFormRenderer(framework=..., include_framework_assets=..., asset_mode=...) is the renderer behind render_form_html(); .render_form_from_model(Model, data=None, errors=None, *, submit_url=..., ...) takes the same options. Reuse one instance to render many forms with the same settings.
  • CSRFMode is the enum behind csrf_mode (CSRFMode.REQUIRED_PROVIDER, ...).
  • read_asset_text(path) returns a packaged asset, such as the vendored HTMX, for serving yourself; see Assets.
  • parse_nested_form_data() and flatten_nested_data() convert between the input names (pets[0].name) and nested data, for tests that post raw form data.

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
The classes behind Rule-Based Validation and Live Validation. Everything here is imported from the top-level package:

from pydantic_schemaforms import FormValidator, PhoneRule, NumericRangeRule

Rules run alongside the model's own validation, never instead of it. The built-in rules other than RequiredRule pass an empty value, so an optional field is only checked when it's filled in. A CustomRule function is called for empty values too.

docs.title: Rule classes
docs.text:
Every rule takes message= to replace its default text.

Rule Checks Arguments RequiredRule() The value is present and not blank message MinLengthRule(min_length) At least min_length characters min_length, message MaxLengthRule(max_length) At most max_length characters max_length, message RegexRule(pattern) Matches the regular expression pattern, message, flags EmailRule() Looks like an email address (format only) message EmailDeliverabilityRule() The email's domain exists and accepts mail (a real DNS lookup; server only; needs the email extra) message, timeout (seconds) PhoneRule() Looks like a phone number: 10 to 15 digits, with optional +, spaces, dashes, dots and parentheses message NumericRangeRule(min_value, max_value) A number within the range; either end can be None min_value, max_value, message DateRangeRule(min_date, max_date) A date within the range; dates or "YYYY-MM-DD" strings min_date, max_date, message CustomRule(func) func(value) returns True, or (is_valid, message) validator_func, message

Without message=, EmailDeliverabilityRule reports the lookup's own reason, such as "The domain name example.invalid does not exist."

A rule on its own: PhoneRule().validate("abc") returns (False, "Please enter a valid phone number").

docs.title: FormValidator
docs.text:
A set of rules for a whole form.

Method Does FormValidator() (or create_validator()) Creates an empty set .field(name) The FieldValidator for that field, created on first use .add_cross_field_rule(func) Adds a check of the whole data. func(data) returns (is_valid, {field: message}). .validate(data) Runs every rule. Returns (is_valid, {field: [messages]}).

docs.title: FieldValidator
docs.text:
The rules of one field. Every method returns the validator, so they chain:

rules.field("username").required().min_length(3).max_length(20)
Method Adds .add_rule(rule) Any rule instance .required(message=None) RequiredRule .min_length(n, message=None) / .max_length(n, message=None) MinLengthRule / MaxLengthRule .email(message=None, check_deliverability=False, dns_timeout=None) EmailRule, plus EmailDeliverabilityRule when asked .email_deliverability(message=None, dns_timeout=None) EmailDeliverabilityRule .phone(message=None) PhoneRule .numeric_range(min_val=None, max_val=None, message=None) NumericRangeRule .date_range(min_date=None, max_date=None, message=None) DateRangeRule .regex(pattern, message=None) RegexRule .custom(func, message=None) CustomRule .validate(value) Runs the rules: (is_valid, [messages])

FieldValidator("email") also works on its own, and a ValidationSchema collects several (.add_field(validator)) for a LiveValidator (.build_live_validator()).

docs.title: CrossFieldRules
docs.text:
Ready-made functions for add_cross_field_rule():

Function Checks CrossFieldRules.password_confirmation(password_field="password", confirm_field="confirm_password", message=...) The two fields match; the message goes on the confirmation CrossFieldRules.date_range_validation(start_field, end_field, message=...) The end date is after the start date; the message goes on the end date

docs.title: Single-value checks
docs.text:
Function Returns create_email_validator(check_deliverability=False, dns_timeout=None) A function that checks one email and returns a ValidationResponse create_password_strength_validator(min_length=8) A function that checks a password's length and mix of characters, with warnings and suggestions

ValidationResponse has field_name, is_valid, errors, warnings, suggestions, value and formatted_value, plus to_dict() and to_json().

docs.title: DeliverableEmailStr
docs.text:
An EmailStr type that also does the DNS check as part of Pydantic validation, so a model field is enough:

from pydantic_schemaforms import DeliverableEmailStr, Field, FormModel


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    email: DeliverableEmailStr = Field(title="Email")

validate(), as_api_model() and LiveValidator.for_model() all apply it.

docs.title: LiveValidator
docs.text:
Checks fields on the server as the user types; the Live Validation page shows the whole setup.

Member Does LiveValidator.for_model(*models, debounce_ms=600, config=None) A validator that checks each field of the given models against their own types and constraints .register_field_validator(validator) Adds a FieldValidator's rules for its field .register_schema(schema) Adds every field of a ValidationSchema .register_model_validator(Model) Adds every field of another model, for several forms on one validator .validate_field(name, value) Checks one value: a ValidationResponse .render_field_with_live_validation(...) Renders one input wired to the validation endpoint .render_htmx_script() The script tag that loads HTMX for the page

HTMXValidationConfig sets when checks run and how results look: validate_on_blur (default True), validate_on_change (True), validate_on_input (False), debounce_ms (300), the CSS classes (success_class, error_class, warning_class, loading_class) and whether to show success, warnings and suggestions. validation_response_headers() returns the response headers an endpoint should send with a check's result.

docs.title: Tutorial - User Guide
docs.text:
This tutorial builds a form step by step, from a two-field model to nested sub-forms, layouts and CSRF protection. Each chapter builds on the one before, so reading them in order is the fastest way to learn the library.

Every chapter shows the recommended way first. Alternatives, when there are any, come in collapsed notes or in the Advanced User Guide.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Create a project and add pydantic-schemaforms with uv:

uv init signup-app --bare
cd signup-app
uv add "pydantic-schemaforms[fastapi]"

pydantic-schemaforms needs Python 3.14 or newer: it builds all of its HTML with Python 3.14 template strings (t-strings), which escape every value automatically.

Using Flask instead

Install the flask extra instead of fastapi:

uv add "pydantic-schemaforms[flask]"

Every example in these docs that has a route shows a FastAPI and a Flask tab. Pick Flask once and every example on the site switches to it.

Using pip instead 
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install "pydantic-schemaforms[fastapi]"
Email fields

Pydantic's EmailStr type needs the email-validator package. Add the email extra if any of your forms use it:

uv add "pydantic-schemaforms[fastapi,email]"

docs.title: Run the examples
docs.text:
Every example in the tutorial is a complete file. Save it as main.py and run it:

FastAPIFlask 
uv run fastapi dev main.py

uv run flask --app main run --debug

Then open the page the example serves, for example http://127.0.0.1:8000/signup (FastAPI) or http://127.0.0.1:5000/signup (Flask).

The live demo at https://pydantic-schemaforms.devsetgo.com shows every input, layout and validation the library supports.

docs.title: Chapters
docs.text:
1. First Form: declare a form and render it.
  2. Handling Submissions: validate a POST and show errors.
  3. Fields and Inputs: titles, input types, defaults, choices.
  4. Validation: constraints, field and form validators.
  5. Nested Forms and Lists: sub-forms and repeating items.
  6. Layouts: sections, tabs, accordions and a step wizard.
  7. Styling: Bootstrap, Material or plain HTML.
  8. CSRF Protection: protect forms behind a login.

docs.title: CSRF Protection
docs.text:
If your site logs users in with a cookie, any other website can make a visitor's browser post to your forms, and the browser sends the cookie along. That's cross-site request forgery (CSRF). The defense is a secret token: your form carries it in a hidden field, and your route refuses any submission that doesn't send it back.

pydantic-schemaforms renders the hidden field. Your app creates the token, keeps it in the session and checks it, because only your app knows its sessions.

FastAPIFlask 
import hmac
import secrets

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, html, render_form_html_async


class TransferForm(FormModel):
    to_account: str = Field(title='To account')
    amount: int = Field(title='Amount', ge=1)


app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key='change-me')  # load from your settings


def issue_csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    request.session['csrf_token'] = token
    return token


def csrf_token_is_valid(request: Request, submitted: object) -> bool:
    expected = request.session.get('csrf_token')
    return bool(expected and isinstance(submitted, str)) and hmac.compare_digest(
        expected, submitted
    )


def form_options(request: Request) -> dict:
    return {
        'submit_url': '/transfer',
        'csrf_mode': 'required-provider',
        'csrf_token_provider': issue_csrf_token(request),
        'include_framework_assets': True,
        'asset_mode': 'cdn',
    }


@app.get('/transfer', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def show_transfer(request: Request):
    return await render_form_html_async(TransferForm, **form_options(request))


@app.post('/transfer', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def submit_transfer(request: Request):
    form = await request.form()
    if not csrf_token_is_valid(request, form.get('csrf_token')):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail='Invalid or expired form; reload the page.')

    result = TransferForm.validate(form, **form_options(request))
    if not result.is_valid:
        return await result.render_with_errors_async()

    amount = result.data['amount']
    return html(t'<p>Transferred {amount}.</p>')

import hmac
import secrets

from flask import Flask, abort, request, session

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, html, render_form_html


class TransferForm(FormModel):
    to_account: str = Field(title='To account')
    amount: int = Field(title='Amount', ge=1)


app = Flask(__name__)
app.secret_key = 'change-me'  # load from your settings


def issue_csrf_token() -> str:
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    session['csrf_token'] = token
    return token


def csrf_token_is_valid(submitted: object) -> bool:
    expected = session.get('csrf_token')
    return bool(expected and isinstance(submitted, str)) and hmac.compare_digest(
        expected, submitted
    )


def form_options() -> dict:
    return {
        'submit_url': '/transfer',
        'csrf_mode': 'required-provider',
        'csrf_token_provider': issue_csrf_token(),
        'include_framework_assets': True,
        'asset_mode': 'cdn',
    }


@app.get('/transfer')
def show_transfer():
    return render_form_html(TransferForm, **form_options())


@app.post('/transfer')
def submit_transfer():
    if not csrf_token_is_valid(request.form.get('csrf_token')):
        abort(403, 'Invalid or expired form; reload the page.')

    result = TransferForm.validate(request.form, **form_options())
    if not result.is_valid:
        return result.render_with_errors()

    amount = result.data['amount']
    return html(t'<p>Transferred {amount}.</p>')

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. issue_csrf_token() makes a random token and stores it in the session.
  2. csrf_mode="required-provider" with csrf_token_provider= renders it as a hidden csrf_token field. The required-provider mode refuses to render without a token, so a missing one is caught at once instead of silently shipping an unprotected form.
  3. The POST route checks the token first, with hmac.compare_digest so the comparison takes the same time whatever the input, and answers 403 when it doesn't match.
  4. validate() gets the same options, so a re-rendered form carries a new token. The token isn't a model field, so it never appears in result.data.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: You need CSRF protection for forms that change something (create, update, delete, buy) on a site that identifies users by cookie. You usually don't for APIs that authenticate with an Authorization header instead of cookies, or for read-only pages.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Keep the session secret (secret_key) out of your code, and long and random.
  • Serve the site over HTTPS.
  • Never log the token values.
  • Use required-provider; csrf_field_name= changes the hidden field's name if your app already uses a different one.
Other CSRF modes

csrf_mode also accepts "off" (the default: no hidden field) and "field-only", which renders the field without requiring a provider. It exists for debugging and is only allowed together with debug=True. CSRFMode.REQUIRED_PROVIDER and the other enum values work the same as the strings.

That's the end of the tutorial. You can now build, validate, arrange, style and protect forms. From here:

  • the Recipes have complete forms to copy;
  • the Advanced User Guide covers live validation, data tables, JSON APIs and more;
  • the Reference lists every input, layout and option.

docs.title: Fields and Inputs
docs.text:
Each field on the model becomes one input. Most of the time the field's type is enough to pick the right input; Field() adds the label, help text and anything else the form needs.

from datetime import date
from enum import Enum
from typing import Literal

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel


class Plan(str, Enum):
    free = 'free'
    team = 'team'
    enterprise = 'enterprise'


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    name: str = Field(title='Full name', min_length=2, ui_autofocus=True)
    email: str = Field(title='Email', ui_element='email', ui_placeholder='you@example.com')
    birthday: date | None = Field(None, title='Birthday')
    plan: Plan = Field(Plan.free, title='Plan', description='You can change plans at any time.')
    team_size: int = Field(1, title='Team size', ge=1, le=500)
    contact: Literal['email', 'phone'] = Field('email', title='Contact me by', ui_element='radio')
    bio: str = Field('', title='About you', ui_element='textarea')
    newsletter: bool = Field(False, title='Send me the newsletter')

Use it with the routes from Handling Submissions; only the model changes. You get a text box for the name, an email box, a date picker, a dropdown of plans, a number box limited to 1–500, two radio buttons, a text area and a checkbox.

docs.title: The type picks the input
docs.text:
Without a ui_element, the input comes from the field's type:

Field type Input str Text box int, float Number box (for a Decimal, set ui_element="decimal" or "currency") bool Checkbox date Date picker datetime Date and time picker time Time picker EmailStr Email box AnyUrl URL box Enum, Literal[...] Dropdown of the values list[Enum], list[Literal[...]] Multi-select Another FormModel A sub-form; see Nested Forms and Lists list of a FormModel A repeating sub-form

plan: Plan above needs nothing else: its dropdown lists free, team and enterprise, and the submitted value comes back as a Plan.

docs.title: Choosing a different input
docs.text:
Set ui_element when the type alone isn't enough: "email" for a plain str holding an email address, "textarea" for longer text, "radio" to show a few choices side by side instead of a dropdown, "password", "color", "slider", "tags", "file" and many more.

Input Types lists every ui_element with all of its options.

docs.title: Labels, help text and placeholders
docs.text:
Setting Shows as title="Full name" The label. Without it, the field name is used: team_size becomes "Team Size". description="..." Help text under the input ui_placeholder="you@example.com" Grey hint text inside an empty input ui_autofocus=True The cursor starts in this field

Help text and error messages are linked to their input for screen readers, and every input gets a label; see Accessibility.

docs.title: Required and optional fields
docs.text:
A field without a default is required: the form marks its label with * and won't validate without it. Give it a default to make it optional, or None with an Optional type when "no answer" is a valid answer:

birthday: date | None = Field(None, title="Birthday")

An optional dropdown gets an empty first choice, and submitting it empty gives None.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text: Pydantic constraints such as min_length, max_length, ge, le and pattern do two things: they're checked when the form is submitted, and they become HTML attributes (minlength, min, max, pattern) so the browser can catch mistakes before the form is sent. team_size above only accepts 1 to 500 either way. The next chapter, Validation, covers them in detail.

docs.title: Defaults and pre-filled forms
docs.text:
A fresh form starts from the field defaults: the team size shows 1, the plan is free, the radio button is on "email".

To show existing values, for example to edit a saved record, pass them as form_data:

from models import SignupForm

from pydantic_schemaforms import render_form_html

saved = {'name': 'Ada Lovelace', 'email': 'ada@example.com', 'plan': 'team', 'team_size': 12}

form_html = render_form_html(SignupForm, form_data=saved, submit_url='/signup')

When you pass form_data, it's used as is: fields you leave out are empty, not filled with their defaults. That's what you want when you re-render a submission, where an unticked checkbox is simply missing.

Widget-specific options

Some inputs take extra settings through ui_options, for example the number of rows of a text area or the choices and labels of a select built from a plain str field:

bio: str = Field("", ui_element="textarea", ui_options={"rows": 6})
size: str = Field(
    "m",
    ui_element="select",
    ui_options={"choices": [
        {"value": "s", "label": "Small"},
        {"value": "m", "label": "Medium"},
    ]},
)

Input Types lists every option of every input. Use ui_options only for presentation: a limit such as min/max must be a Pydantic constraint (ge/le) so it's actually enforced.

Next: Validation.

docs.title: First Form
docs.text:
A form is a Pydantic model. Subclass FormModel, declare the fields, and render it.

FastAPIFlask 
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, render_form_html_async


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    name: str = Field(title='Full name')
    email: str = Field(title='Email', ui_element='email')


app = FastAPI()


@app.get('/signup', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def show_signup():
    return await render_form_html_async(
        SignupForm,
        submit_url='/signup',
        include_framework_assets=True,
        asset_mode='cdn',
    )

from flask import Flask

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, render_form_html


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    name: str = Field(title='Full name')
    email: str = Field(title='Email', ui_element='email')


app = Flask(__name__)


@app.get('/signup')
def show_signup():
    return render_form_html(
        SignupForm,
        submit_url='/signup',
        include_framework_assets=True,
        asset_mode='cdn',
    )

Run it and open /signup: you get a styled form with a "Full name" text box, an "Email" box and a submit button.

docs.title: What's going on
docs.text:
SignupForm(FormModel) is an ordinary Pydantic model. FormModel adds the form rendering and validation on top, so the same class can still be used anywhere a Pydantic model can.

Field(title=...) works like Pydantic's Field and adds the form settings. title becomes the field's label; without it the label comes from the field name (email becomes "Email").

ui_element="email" picks the input type. Without it, the library picks one from the field's type: str gets a text box, bool a checkbox, date a date picker. Fields and Inputs covers this in detail.

render_form_html_async() returns the form as an HTML string, including its labels, inline validation script and the submit button. The FastAPI example uses the async version so rendering doesn't block the event loop; Flask uses the plain render_form_html().

submit_url is required: it's where the form posts to. The library never guesses a default.

include_framework_assets=True, asset_mode="cdn" adds the <link> and <script> tags that load Bootstrap from a CDN, so this one string is a working page. In a real app your page template already loads Bootstrap: drop these two options and put the form into your template.

Putting the form in your own page template

render_form_html() returns a plain string of trusted HTML. In a Jinja template, mark it safe so Jinja doesn't escape it:

<main class="container">
  <h1>Sign up</h1>
  {{ form_html | safe }}
</main>

Never build the page around it with an f-string if the page also shows anything the user typed; see Handling Submissions. The Jinja template recipe has a complete example.

Rendering from the model class

SignupForm.render_form(submit_url="/signup") does the same as render_form_html(SignupForm, submit_url="/signup"). The docs use render_form_html() throughout because it has an async version.

Next: Handling Submissions.

docs.title: Handling Submissions
docs.text:
Add a POST route that validates what was submitted. If anything is wrong, the form comes back with the user's values kept and an error under each field that failed. If everything is valid, you get the data as a plain dictionary.

FastAPIFlask 
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, html, render_form_html_async


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    name: str = Field(title='Full name', min_length=2)
    email: str = Field(title='Email', ui_element='email')


app = FastAPI()
RENDER_OPTIONS = {'include_framework_assets': True, 'asset_mode': 'cdn'}


@app.get('/signup', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def show_signup():
    return await render_form_html_async(SignupForm, submit_url='/signup', **RENDER_OPTIONS)


@app.post('/signup', response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def submit_signup(request: Request):
    result = SignupForm.validate(await request.form(), submit_url='/signup', **RENDER_OPTIONS)
    if not result.is_valid:
        return await result.render_with_errors_async()

    name = result.data['name']
    return html(t'<p>Thanks for signing up, {name}!</p>')

from flask import Flask, request

from pydantic_schemaforms import Field, FormModel, html, render_form_html


class SignupForm(FormModel):
    name: str = Field(title='Full name', min_length=2)
    email: str = Field(title='Email', ui_element='email')


app = Flask(__name__)
RENDER_OPTIONS = {'include_framework_assets': True, 'asset_mode': 'cdn'}


@app.get('/signup')
def show_signup():
    return render_form_html(SignupForm, submit_url='/signup', **RENDER_OPTIONS)
